reasons: Deviation is correctly characterized: § 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause that neither grants Customer an affiliate/M&A assignment carve-out nor restricts Vendor assignment, and the Agreement is silent on change of control.

The redline is additive and leaves the original sentence intact, adding exactly the three preferred-position elements: Customer assignment to affiliate/successor without consent, Vendor assignment only with Customer consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, and confirmation that Customer's change of control is not an assignment and gives Vendor no termination or re-pricing right.
'Notwithstanding the foregoing' properly overrides the existing 'no other person shall acquire or have any rights' language, so the inserted carve-out is operative rather than conflicting.

Party references are used correctly (Company as Customer, HDI as Vendor), and the comment accurately describes the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback in the required concise first-person-plural tone.
